per_proof_checks.mathematical_check: The public argument gives the balanced isometry, skew isometric J_symp and the correct final physical formula J_E(f,g)=(Lambda^-1 g,-Lambda f), with the correct Sobolev dual pairing. An intermediate C_bal^-1 tuple is mistranscribed (R1); the isometric conjugation concept and final formula independently supply the needed bounded/skew properties. The free Fourier matrix has determinant one, bounded even entries and a continuous zero quotient; integrating the 2x2 symplectic identity against balanced L2 vectors proves conservation without a zero-frequency trace or rough generator derivative. For real b, the multiplier bound and absolutely integrable -∫fbu+∫ubf give the force identity for omega. Compact Young increments imply compact U_X-I, and free composition gives a compact endpoint difference. Spatial translations are E-isometries commuting with the free group; weighted Fourier products are L1, so translated pairings tend to zero, compact K sends these weak-null families to norm-zero, and reverse triangle gives ||S+K||>=||S||. Velocity reversal plus the group law gives ||S||>=1. Ordered finite-product telescoping yields a compact difference from the corresponding free product, with no commutation of noisy factors or uniform approximation claim. The new reverse-triangle explanation is correct.

The scalar Z=W(Phi) times a separably valued L2 Ctheta path is strongly measurable and Bochner integrable by E||ZM||<=||Phi||HW ||M||L2Ctheta. The same inequality applied to M^rho-M yields the explicit mean convergence; the supplied covariance-contraction bound controls positive-width source norms. The retained isometry j_src and feature vector v_rho give h=〈j_src Phi,v_rho〉, with the stated fixed-positive-width time continuity and spatial derivatives. Multiplying once by the fixed physical mask gives bounded compact support on finite horizons. Schwartz row Fubini is controlled by the scalar-Gaussian covariance Cauchy-Schwarz and bounded positive-width point variance; test/indicator completion and countable states/rational times identify the full Lipschitz primitive. The generally noncentered combined source and once-only mask are correctly retained.

For fixed positive widths and fixed parameters, the common regularity/ordinary-primitive event gives bounded strongly continuous statewise C_b. The report explicitly transfers omega-force skewness through the free symplectic conjugation and computes the two cancelling terms. It correctly distinguishes omega-skewness from E-Hilbert skew-adjointness, although its aside calling B(b) symmetric as an operator is false (R2). Young sums can be replaced by the statewise integrals with a uniform-continuity error, giving C1 trajectories on the same path set. The public product-rule calculation of omega(Ue,Uf) has derivative zero for arbitrary states; together with the already public free-invariance identity, this supplies physical conservation after conjugation, with no uncountable intersection or rough free-generator derivative. One redundant adjoint-factor display has the sign of the initial free time wrong (R3); the correct bilinear-form conservation derivation and defined P=S(t)US(-s) remain public. No missing source regularity assumption or material target step is identified.

The report reconstructs the real closed constraint g_J: conjugating each real smooth force gives C*J+JC=S(r)*(B*J+JB)S(r)=0; statewise integration and real finite Gaussian sums preserve it; bounded path-space A→A*J+JA sends the L2 Ctheta limit to the same constraint on one path event. Bochner expectation and real c preserve it for D=cM+D_Phi. For V=U_D, the Young increment and its second-order remainder cancel the linear g_J term in V*JV. The report lists every remaining remainder/cross term, and its later paragraph correctly uses h^(3theta),h^(4theta)<=h^(2theta) for h<=1 (earlier exponent-comparison wording is wrong, R4). Thus the public mesh sum tends to zero because 2theta>1, giving conservation. The free-invariance step and ||J||=1 imply ||P||>=1. Invertibility is separately obtained from local Neumann pieces/products, not conservation alone in infinite dimension. Deterministic c=0, zero covariance and the fixed-delta fast-noise instance preserve their stated nonuniform scope.

The original pullback factor delta^(a-2)delta^2delta^-a=1 gives an isometry; its adjoint is contractive and phi_m=delta^-a/2 T_m* i_I Phi is finite for fixed delta without a uniform control-radius claim. The completed F mean compresses to the E compact-valued Lr mean with the stated 2<r<2/a and 1-1/r>theta; compact conjugation, affine pullback and constant stopping give the Ctheta compact primitive. Rank-zero full-F covariance with g_delta is compressed through the true intertwining, retaining both constant columns until compression. Dividing g_delta>0 gives delta^(a/2), not sqrt(delta), in the unscaled covariance. Orthogonal T_mT_m* removes only the slow-noise component perpendicular to the fast range: every M_m linear statistic is a limit in that first chaos, so its covariance with the orthogonal component vanishes. Multiplying by delta^-a/2 identifies the stopped mean direction exactly, without a new independent copy or an unstopped identity past ell_m. The compact endpoint lower bound applies to this fixed-parameter compact path even without a Hamiltonian/Gaussian premise; an empty cell gives I. All required scaling and completion deductions are public.

report_notes.disposition: The tuple fed to C_bal^-1 must be in balanced L2 coordinates. The reported inner tuple is already the physical output and applying C_bal^-1 again would give the wrong weights/domain. The report otherwise correctly gives the balanced isometry, conjugation construction and final physical tuple/duality, so the required form/weight deduction remains public. Source uses C_bal^-1 J_symp C_bal correctly.

report_notes.old: B(b) is symmetric (it is the force (0,bu) with symmetric multiplication contribution)
report_notes.new: Multiplication by the real b has a symmetric duality pairing; the force B(b) itself need not be symmetric or skew-adjoint in the E Hilbert norm. Its relevant identity is B(b)^*J_E+J_EB(b)=0.
report_notes.contrary_calculation: A nonzero force B(b)(u,v)=(0,bu) is bounded and nilpotent with B(b)^2=0. A bounded self-adjoint nilpotent operator would be zero, since ||Bz||^2=〈z,B^2z〉=0. Thus symmetry of the scalar multiplication pairing is not Hilbert self-adjointness of the force block.
report_notes.disposition: The report gives the correct explicit omega-force cancellation and its conjugation transfer independently of this erroneous aside; source distinguishes omega skewness correctly. No source fix or absent conservation deduction follows.

report_notes.classification: report-only initial-time sign in an adjoint display
report_notes.disposition: P_D=S_E(t)U S_E(-s), so the first adjoint factor has -s. The source has no such incorrect display. The report independently derives omega(Ue,Uf)=omega(e,f) for arbitrary states, states free invariance, and explicitly invokes both to pass to the physical flow; that complete bilinear-form deduction is available despite the redundant sign transcription. Do not use the wrong displayed product as a standalone equality.

report_notes.classification: report-only exponent-inequality wording slip, corrected elsewhere in the same public account
report_notes.new: order h^(3theta) and h^(4theta), each bounded by h^(2theta) for 0<h<=1 (or by a fixed-horizon constant times h^(2theta))
report_notes.disposition: The exponents themselves satisfy 3theta>2theta and 4theta>2theta. The report later explicitly gives the correct power inequalities at h<=1, and its mesh-remainder calculation uses that correct domination. Source states O(h^(2theta)) without the false exponent comparison. No missing partition argument or source repair.
